verses.text: "Brothers and fathers, listen now while I defend myself."
When they heard him speak to them in the Hebrew language, they became even quieter. Then Paul said,

"I am a Jew. I was born in Tarsus in Cilicia, but I grew up here in this city. I studied under Gamaliel. He taught me very carefully the law of our ancestors. I was eager to serve God, just as all of you are today.
I attacked the people who followed the Way, even to the point of death. I arrested men and women and threw them into prison.

The high priest and all the council of elders can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish brothers in Damascus. So I went there to arrest the believers and bring them back to Jerusalem to be punished.
As I was on my way and came near Damascus, at about midday, a bright light from the sky suddenly flashed around me.
I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, 'Saul, Saul, why are you attacking me?'
I asked, 'Who are you, Lord?' He said to me, 'I am Jesus of Nazareth, the one you are attacking.'
The men with me saw the light and were afraid, but they did not understand the voice of the one speaking to me.
I asked, 'What should I do, Lord?' The Lord said, 'Get up and go into Damascus. There you will be told everything you have been chosen to do.'
The bright light had made me blind, so the men with me led me by the hand into Damascus.
A man named Ananias came to see me. He was a godly man who obeyed the law, and all the Jews living in Damascus spoke well of him.
He stood beside me and said, 'Brother Saul, see again!' At that very moment I could see him.
Then he said, 'The God of our ancestors has chosen you to know his will. He chose you to see the Righteous One and to hear his voice.
You will tell everyone about what you have seen and heard.
So what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptised and wash your sins away, calling on his name.'
Later I went back to Jerusalem. While I was praying in the temple, I saw a vision.
I saw the Lord, and he said to me, 'Hurry! Leave Jerusalem quickly, because the people here will not accept what you tell them about me.'
I said, 'Lord, they know that I went from one synagogue to another to put believers in prison and beat them.
And when Stephen, who spoke for you, was killed, I was standing there. I agreed with it, and I guarded the coats of the men who were killing him.'
Then the Lord said to me, 'Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles.'"
The crowd listened to Paul until he said this. Then they shouted, "Get rid of him! He is not fit to live!"
They shouted, threw off their coats and threw dust into the air.
So the commander ordered Paul to be taken into the army building. He told his soldiers to whip Paul and question him, to find out why the people were shouting against him like this.
When they had tied him up to be whipped, Paul said to the officer standing there, "Is it legal for you to whip a Roman citizen who has not even been found guilty?"
When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, "Be careful what you do! This man is a Roman citizen."
The commander came and asked Paul, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?" Paul answered, "Yes."
The commander said, "I had to pay a lot of money to become a citizen." Paul said, "But I was born a citizen."
At once the men who were about to question him moved away. The commander was afraid too, because he had put a Roman citizen in chains.

The next day the commander wanted to know exactly why the Jews were accusing Paul. So he set him free and ordered the leading priests and the whole council to meet. Then he brought Paul and made him stand in front of them.
